sourceActivityToPaper.source: 3.1 Notice and Wonder: The Isometric Grid
sourceActivityToPaper.key: Six equilateral sectors of 60° around vertex O; equal-length 60° basis e1=(1,0), e2=(1/2,sqrt(3)/2); slanted nonperpendicular axes
Image I has constant (+2,-1) for all vertices so it is a translation; Image II has (+2,-1),(+2,-1),(0,-1) so NOT one translation.

privateTeacherRubric.Scoring: 0 incorrect/absent;1 partially accurate;2 precise labelled construction/justification per criterion; teacher notes and final points recorded OFFLINE only.

Criteria.Skill: Triangular/isometric grid correctly displays six 60-degree sectors and recognizes nonperpendicular equal-length basis
Three separately reconstructed transformations correctly labelled with all vertex correspondences and retained side lengths
Isometric 60-degree axial rotation exact and clearly explained to partner without treating axes as Cartesian
First-party Cool-down accepts only uniform displacement vectors for Image I; rejects Image II with all three vectors and drawing/reproducible explanation

correct: Six equilateral sectors of 60° at O, e1 and e2 nonperpendicular
T image (3,0),(5,0),(4,2) separately from original triangle
Cool-down Image I translates all three vertices (+2,-1), II does not
equivalent: Teacher accepts mathematically equivalent labelled diagrams and exact fraction/radical basis expression
Written or spoken complete explanation of square-grid rigid transformations with correct coordinates
Image I described as move 2 right,1 down or displacement vector (2,-1)
wrong: Assuming isometric slanted axes are perpendicular 90°
Applying rotation to already translated triangle instead of original
Clockwise quarter-turn from A(1,1) to (1,-1) as if CCW
Image II falsely classified a translation because only A/B vectors match
malformed: Unlabelled A′ B′ C′ or missing a vertex
Only the word translation without three displacement vectors for Cool-down
Missing or blank triangular-sector grid observation
boundary: Isometric basis components in Cartesian form may use exact radical sqrt(3)/2 rather than rounded 0.866...
Axial coordinates describe a nonorthogonal lattice, not ordinary x/y point distances
Any correct diagram orientation equivalent under a specified isometric basis is acceptable
Text-only accessible geometric description must identify each image and correspondences
A half turn or reflection also preserves lengths but is not a translation unless all vertex displacements match
